In addition, TCC samples prepared with the 45- 18/52 DE-EE0010241 Nicolas Gaillard 53µm Ag-PMMA microsphere fillers repeatedly resulted in nominal thicknesses above 100µm as indicated by a digital Vernier caliper, likely due to the combined effects of outliers in the size distribution, agglomeration of spheres, and the relatively low pressure across the large sample area (approximately 0.5 bars) during the room-temperature lamination. Operators were limited in their capacity to increase lamination pressure due to the lack of specialized equipment. As such, larger microsphere fillers (Cospheric PMMAMS-AG-1.2, 95% of which within the 500-520µm range) were used to prepare supplementary free-standing TCC (FS-TCC) samples to assist in the evaluation of WVTRs. Despite the range of WVTRs (thickness-dependent) measured across samples with varying thicknesses, the permeabilities (a thickness-independent metric) facilitated the comparison of the results. Free-standing laminate samples (i.e., epoxy only and without microsphere fillers) were prepared using metal shims (350µm or 500µm) placed along the edges of the acrylic substrates to dictate the thickness and served as a benchmark to measure any changes to WVTR due to the inclusion of microsphere fillers. These samples were analyzed at NREL as received (0hr) or after 1,000 hours of accelerated damp heat aging (85°C, 85% R.H.). The WVTR measurement procedure followed IEC 62788-6-2.131 A Mocon Aquatran model SRT051-100 and Mocon Permatran-W 3/31 instruments were used following the manufacturer’s instructions for calibration. These systems were modified with remote cells capable of testing within 5 ˚C to 85 ˚C. Damp heat aging (85 ˚C, 85% R.H.) of FS-TCC and laminate samples was conducted using a temperature/humidity environmental test chamber (Thermal Product Solutions, Blue-M FRS-361F). The WVTR measurements for Aluzine epoxy laminates (epoxy only: thickness of 350µm and 510µm) and Aluzine TCCs (45-53µm or 500-520µm Ag-PMMA microspheres + Aluzine epoxy) are summarized in Table 5. First, an as-synthesized laminate with a thickness of 510 ± 30µm served as the benchmark, measuring a WVTR of 1.48 ± 0.074 g/m2/day, corresponding to a permeability of 0.75 ± 0.058 g·mm/m2/day. Compared to the benchmarks set by the laminate samples, an as-synthesized FS-TCC sample with 500- 520µm Ag-PMMA microsphere inclusions (thickness: 550 µm ± 25µm) sustains comparable WVTR and permeability of 1.37 ± 0.069 g/m2/day and 0.75 ± 0.051 19/52 DE-EE0010241 Nicolas Gaillard g·mm/m2/day, respectively.
